profile.address: 1400 East Devon Avenue, Elk Grove Village, IL 60007
profile.reading:
This is Digital Realty facility CH3, at 1400 East Devon Avenue, Elk Grove Village, IL. Digital Realty's own property listing for CH3, fetched this session, lists the building at 305,500 square feet.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is part of Digital Realty's Chicago metro footprint, a cluster of suburban buildings near O'Hare International Airport in Elk Grove Village and neighboring Franklin Park, in addition to the much larger Lakeside Technology Center downtown at 350 East Cermak Road. Digital Realty markets its Chicago properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Dallas, Silicon Valley, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform. The company does not publish a consolidated IT power rating in megawatts for individual Chicago buildings in the sources reviewed this session.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage. Illinois has offered data center-specific state tax incentives, administered by the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity, that local officials have credited with helping draw large colocation and hyperscale investment to the Chicago metro.

reading.body:
Digital Realty's CH3 facility in Elk Grove Village contains 305,500 square feet of data center space with N+1 UPS redundancy, but its critical IT power capacity remains unconfirmed from tier-1 sources.

This facility is part of a multi-building cluster near Chicago's O'Hare airport. Digital Realty operates at least four confirmed buildings in the metro area, with CH3 in Elk Grove Village and three additional facilities (ORD12, ORD13, ORD14) in neighboring Franklin Park on the same street. The clustering suggests shared infrastructure and optimized logistics for a dense deployment.

The data does not specify the megawatt capacity serving this building, which is the critical variable for understanding its role in regional AI compute availability. Square footage alone cannot predict power draw. Without confirmed MW from Digital Realty's engineering specifications or utility filings, the facility's actual constraint on compute scaling in the Chicago metro remains unknown. The N+1 UPS redundancy confirms backup power exists but not its duration or sufficiency for modern high-density AI workloads.
